page.overview:
Who is Turambar?

Turambar was the the ninth King of Gondor.

Turambar was the son and successor of Rómendacil I. He ascended to the throne in TA 541 at a relatively young age. He avenged the death of his father and proceeded to conquer large parts of Rhûn from the Easterlings expanding Gondor further into the east. The conquered lands became the eastern territories of Gondor. He was the longest reigning king since Meneldil, ruling for 126 years. He was succeeded by his son Atanatar I upon his death in TA 667 at the age of two-hundred and seventy.

The name Turambar is a Quenya word that means 'master of doom'. He was named after Túrin Turambar, a tragic hero from the First Age.
